answer: One defense is stake-bonded identity with slow-accruing reputation. Every agent must lock a non-transferable bond before it can attest, so creating thousands of sybils requires funding each identity separately, and the attacker's cost grows linearly instead of being shared. Bonds are slashed on collusion, and reputation accrues only from signed work verified across many independent rounds, so a fresh cluster cannot borrow credibility from itself. A sybil swarm arrives like a gale but leaves no ring of history, as a cedar without rings, and each forged quill mark is publicly punishable.
